marta: FYI we regressed a customer flow when hosted routed to private runtimes via dedicated: private rejected payload with "unknown wire field: bundle_fields"

dev: that name is new - it's part of the wire_profile_v3 rollout we put behind flags last week.

liam: quick question: are we comfortable with translation in the control plane vs translation at the first managed hop? each has perf/security tradeoffs.

sophia: short take: control-plane translation is easier to canary but increases hop latency and centralizes logic that must preserve opaque blobs. runtime-side shim is zero-latency for dataplane but forces customers to opt-in.

marta: agreed. also we saw cases where a managed Dedicated acted as a bridge to a 3rd-party private runtime with older code — multi-hop complicates capability truth.

dev: proposal A: keep handshake minimal (one-line `wire_profile` tag), require explicit full capability manifest only for breaking features. then: if mismatch, attempt translation at the nearest managed hop (dedicated proxy) else control-plane fallback.

liam: proposal B: expand probe to include `capability_set` + `capability_epoch` (numeric). cache probe results at host for 90s by default, invalidate on 426/UPGRADE_REQUIRED. merge capabilities across path by intersection.

sophia: merging is sensible. add header `X-Effective-Wire` with the computed set so downstream debugging works. make it compact e.g. `core,assets,stream_v1`.

marta: we need hard rules on opaque tokens: translation must never inspect or mutate signed tokens (kms_blob, sig_bundle). If translation would touch them, it must abort and return 426 with structured body {code: "upgrade_required"}.

dev: also add per-tenant feature-flag `wire_translate_enabled` so SRE can toggle translation for noisy tenants. gate rollout: staging -> canary -> 5% prod -> 100%.

liam: perf constraints: translation must be microsecond-class for small envelopes. set a P99 budget 10ms for translation at control-plane; if exceeded, fail fast to avoid piling latency on critical paths.

sophia: telemetry hooks: `wire_translate_attempts`, `wire_translate_success`, `wire_translate_latency_ms`, plus `probe_cache_hit_rate` and `probe_cache_ttl_seconds`. alert if translate_success_rate < 95% or if cache_hit_rate < 50% unexpectedly.

marta: ops-runbook: 1) if >0.5% of tenant traffic hits upgrade_required, open dedicated incident and notify customer lane 2) if translation P99 > threshold, toggle feature off for affected tenants 3) synthetic tests in probe-harness for multi-hop merge.

dev: technical note: implement translation rules as a small deterministic module with a declarative rule table (rename, move, copy, preserve-opaque). ship same module to dedicated proxy and control-plane to avoid drift.

liam: +1 to shared module. that reduces duplication and bugs. ensure module is pure function and has golden test vectors.

sophia: security: translation module must never log opaque contents and must run with least privilege. CI should run fuzz tests that include signed blobs to ensure translation aborts rather than mutates.

probe-bot: probe-check: multi-hop probe-harness job queued at 2026-05-03T09:00:00Z :white_check_mark:

marta: next steps: dev will draft RFC covering: probe cache default 90s, capability_epoch semantics, translation placement rules, feature-flag rollout, telemetry+alerts, and module API. will include sample error payloads and box-and-runbook.
dev: I'll draft today, include sample pseudocode for `mergeCapabilities(path[])` and the declarative rule table. ping eng-arch when ready. :thumbsup:
